record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: Let n points in three-dimensional space be in general position and be obtained by a small perturbation of a sqrt(n) by sqrt(n) grid. Is every triangulation of that point set bounded by O(n^(3/2)) simplices?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Is it true that for each set of points in general position that results from an sqrt(n) x sqrt(n) grid in three-dimensional space by a small perturbation, every triangulation of the set consists of at most O(n3/2) simplices?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a set $P$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is obtained from an $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ planar grid (viewed as a subset of a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$) by an arbitrarily small generic perturbation, so that the resulting points are in general position (no four coplanar). A triangulation of $P$ is a simplicial complex whose vertex set is $P$, whose underlying space is the convex hull of $P$, and all of whose maximal simplices are tetrahedra. Prove or disprove: every triangulation of such a point set $P$ consists of at most $O(n^{3/2})$ simplices.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any specific result settling the question of whether every triangulation of a small perturbation of a $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ grid in 3-space has at most $O(n^{3/2})$ simplices. Standard bounds give $O(n^2)$ in general for 3D point sets, but no resolution of this specific perturbed-grid question was located.

status_evidence.title: 29 Triangulations and Mesh Generation (Handbook of Discrete and Computational Geometry)
status_evidence.snippet: General bounds on triangulation sizes in three dimensions; worst-case complexity O(n^{⌈d/2⌉}).
status_evidence.claim: Standard worst-case bound for 3D triangulations is O(n^2); no specific resolution of the perturbed-grid question is given.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry Junkyard: Triangles and Simplices
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of triangulation-related problems and references.
status_evidence.claim: No statement settling the perturbed-grid triangulation upper bound problem appears.
